Personal hygiene
• Washing hands thoroughly before preparing food, after visiting the toilet and after emptying the rubbish bin
• Never licking ﬁngers or utensils and put them back into food
• Washing hands after blowing or touching the nose whilst handling food
• Keeping nails clean and hair out of food
• Wearing a clean apron
• Not handling food during periods of illness, e.g., heavy cold, sickness or diarrhea
• Covering all cuts, spots and pimples, particularly on the hands, with a waterproof dressing and replacing it often
• Wearing rubber gloves when emptying cat litter trays.

The question of whether moderate or occasional alcohol consumption is safe during pregnancy has been widely debated.
Currently, there is little evidence that modest drinking (<10 units per week) has any harmful effects. In a systematic review of
the evidence, reported in the National Institute of Health and Clinical Excellence (NICE) 2008 guidelines “Antenatal care: routine
